subject: Residency risk treatment & cutover schedule — EU/APAC private deployment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Suzanne Park <suzanne@fintech.co>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Residency risk treatment & cutover schedule — EU/APAC private deployment

Suzanne / team,

Thanks again for walking through the private deployment requirements last week. Attached is our proposed risk-treatment packet and an initial cutover schedule for the two-region private topology (primary: EU, standby: APAC). This thread captures a few decision points we need from FinTech Co. to lock the timeline:

- KMS custody: customer-managed KMS in EU (preferred) vs. Redwood-managed with HSM + dual-region replication (tradeoffs documented in attachment).
- Control plane: proposal is customer-controlled control plane sitting in EU with API endpoints pinned to EU. We recommend a read-only degraded mode in APAC on failover to limit cross-border writes.
- Failover mode: automated region-level fallback for network outages (stateless requests only) + manual switchover for stateful/consistency-sensitive workflows.
- Auditing & retention: continuous audit logs held in EU for 90 days; on-request extended retention available under SOW.

Requested action from FinTech Co.: please confirm the KMS preference and whether you can accept the proposed manual switchover window (30 mins SLA for operator acknowledgement, up to 2 hours to complete cross-region cutover). If we get signoff by Thu 2026-11-05 we can schedule the dry-run the week of Nov 16.

Attachments: residency-risk-register-v2.xlsx (risk treatments + owners), eu-apac-cutover-schedule-v1.pdf (timeline), kms-options-summary.docx (KMS tradeoffs).

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Suzanne Park <suzanne@fintech.co>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 13:28:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Residency risk treatment & cutover schedule — EU/APAC private deployment

Marissa,

Thanks for the packet — this is a helpful start. A few initial comments from our end: 

1) KMS: our security team prefers customer-managed KMS in EU with no key material leaving the jurisdiction. We need to confirm if Redwood can integrate a BYOK flow with our cloud provider (we're on GCP-Europe). Is there a step-by-step for the key exchange and rotation scheme?

2) Audit logs: EU retention 90 days is OK, but we need proof-of-immutability and a copy to our internal SIEM pipeline (Splunk). We will need a sample audit export for SOC review.

3) Failover behavior: read-only in APAC is acceptable for sessionless workloads. Our payments flow is stateful and cannot be manually cut over during business hours in APAC — are you proposing a DNS-based switchover or a routing-layer change? We need clarity on RTO/RPO for the payments lane.

I'll loop in our ITSec folks separately (cc'ing itsec@acme.com for the SOC intake). Once we have the KMS integration note and a short audit-export sample, we can confirm signoff on the cutover window.

—Suzanne
VP Product, FinTech Co.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Suzanne Park <suzanne@fintech.co>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Residency risk treatment & cutover schedule — EU/APAC private deployment

Suzanne — thanks, great questions. Answering each point below and outlining next steps.

1) KMS/BYOK: Redwood supports a BYOK flow for GCP KMS. We will provide an integration checklist and an HSM-backed exchange process: customer generates key material in GCP EU, we validate the key thumbprint over a secure channel, and Redwood stores only the key reference (not the raw material) when customer opts for BYOK. Rotation can be scheduled; we suggest quarterly rotation with a rolling-reload process. See kms-options-summary.docx (section 2). Action: Naomi will send the step-by-step checklist and a sample terraform snippet by EOD tomorrow.

2) Audit exports: we can deliver an immutable audit archive (WORM) exported to a customer-controlled GCS bucket in EU. The archive includes signed manifests for tamper evidence. Naomi will prepare a 24-hr sample export (redacted) for Splunk ingestion. Action: Naomi (owner).

3) Failover & payments lane: for stateful payments we recommend a controlled manual cutover. Technical approach: 
   - Primary routing remains EU (regional affinity).
   - APAC hosts a warm-standby read-only runtime; on network failure, sessionless traffic can be served from APAC automatically.
   - Payments traffic (stateful) will fail open to EU via a routing-layer proxy when possible; if link is saturated we execute an operator-led switchover: operator triggers state replication sync (KV checkpoint) + DNS TTL cutover + route propagation.

RTO/RPO targets we propose for payments lane: RTO 2 hours (operator-led), RPO 5 minutes (KV checkpointing frequency). If FinTech requires stricter RTO we can propose a synchronous replication variant but it incurs ~2-3x cost and additional latency.

4) Compliance evidence: adding a Confluence playbook and a proposed tabletop schedule. We propose a dry-run Nov 17 (EU business hours) to validate the operator-led cutover; that gives your team one week to review.

Next steps: Naomi will follow up with the KMS checklist and sample audit export by EOD 2026-11-03. Karthik/Jonas — can you confirm operator runbook owners and whether the ops team can take the Nov 17 dry-run slot?

Best,
Marissa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
